calendar.impact: The DNR's formal Notice of Violation of Oct 13 reaches its enforcement conference. Line 5 is operating via its temporary bypass; the conference is a regulatory-track event for the reroute, not a flow event today.
calendar.title: Line 5 enforcement conference (Wisconsin DNR)

calendar.impact: Bids close on the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels, the first use of the reserve since Hurricane Sandy in 2012), with deliveries to complete by Nov 13. Bid uptake is a dated measure of how tight the Northeast distillate balance remains into winter.
calendar.title: NEHHOR exchange bids due

calendar.impact: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them. The synthetic return verdict, unscored on zero volume, is carried by these volumes.
calendar.title: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results

calendar.impact: Five analysts surveyed by Reuters (Oct 23) expect another modest December increase; delegates said after the Oct 5 meeting that the November increase was the last before a first-quarter pause. The spread between those two is the meeting's actual risk, carried into the highest settles of the episode.
calendar.title: OPEC+ meeting

calendar.impact: Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data.
calendar.title: Suncor Q3 results

calendar.impact: Vermilion reports the quarter on Nov 4 (announced Oct 21). A smaller read on the basin than the majors, carried for calendar completeness.
calendar.title: Vermilion Q3 results

calendar.impact: MEG reports Q3 on Nov 5 (earnings call Nov 6), confirmed from the company's events calendar on Oct 24. A thermal producer read on the quarter.
calendar.title: MEG Energy Q3 results

calendar.title: NEHHOR exchange deliveries complete

calendar.impact: December's Mainline nowcast opens at naive persistence on November's print (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert). No December judgment call is registered yet. Nominations close at 0700 MST.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close (NOS day)

changes.balance: The confirmed barrel impact of the week's campaign remains zero, while the premium compounded again on Friday on claims rather than incidents. The session's most honest data point is the split inside it: crude ran and the diesel crack fell, the first time since the escalation leg began that products did not confirm the crude bid. Positioning says the length sits in Brent, added before the two largest sessions, which are still uncounted.
changes.body: Brent Dec26 settled Friday at $116.72 (up $3.55, or 3.14 percent), its highest settle since April 29, and WTI Dec26 at $103.27 (up $3.80), closing weekly gains of about 6.2 and 4.3 percent on a same-contract December basis. Heating oil settled essentially flat (down 0.02 percent at $4.9310 per gallon), so the completed diesel crack eased to $105.66 from Thursday's $107.68 while gasoline rose 2.03 percent and carried the 3-2-1 crack up to $59.05. Houthi claims against Abha airport and a refining complex at Jazan on Friday are unconfirmed, with no Saudi comment in the wires checked; the coalition confirmed intercepting a booby-trapped drone toward Khamis Mushait, a third straight day of confirmed interceptions. Positioning as of Oct 20 (released Friday) shows Brent speculative net length building to 241,881 while WTI managed-money net length trimmed to 36,187; the vintage predates Thursday and Friday, so the two biggest sessions of the episode are in no positioning print yet.
changes.conditional: A Saudi statement confirming facility damage, or a named vessel behind the vessel claim -> the premium's claim share converts to a supply event. A quiet weekend and a soft Sunday reopen -> the claim share refunds first. A second session of products lagging crude -> the crack, not the flat price, becomes the story.
changes.delta: Friday settles: Brent Dec26 $116.72 (+$3.55); WTI Dec26 $103.27 (+$3.80). Week: Brent +6.2 percent, WTI +4.3 percent (December basis). Diesel crack $105.66 (was $107.68); 3-2-1 $59.05. COT as of Oct 20: Brent net +241,881; WTI managed-money net +36,187.
changes.source: Reuters market wrap, Oct 23, 2026 (settles; Houthi claims; interception via Saudi Press Agency); AP and Fortune, Oct 23 (weekly gains); CFTC and ICE commitment of traders data, vintage as of Oct 20, released Oct 23; validated crack history refreshed Oct 24
changes.title: Friday settled at the episode highs, and products did not confirm it

changes.balance: The volume is small against the plant's throughput (about a day and a half), and the refiner expects no operational impact, so this is a signal, not a balance entry: governments do not lend reserve crude to refineries whose supply chains are working. The undisclosed cause is the fact that decides its weight.
changes.body: The Department of Energy announced Friday an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude to a Louisiana refinery processing about 264 kb/d, drawn from the West Hackberry site for immediate delivery, to address a crude oil supply disruption affecting the refinery (energy.gov, Oct 23). Borrowed barrels return with a premium. The Department did not state what disrupted deliveries, and the refiner confirmed receipt while saying it does not anticipate operational impacts (Reuters, Oct 23). It is the fourth federal channel opened on the supply balance in eight days, after the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (bids due Oct 27), defence-production refinery funding announced Oct 22, and the sanctions waiver whose first Russian diesel cargo is at sea for New York (arrival estimated Nov 7). Posted exchange contracts are unchanged at 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies, and no award has been published for the Sep 29 round or the Oct 16 re-offer whose proposals were due Oct 21.
changes.conditional: A named cause (pipeline, cargo or unit) -> the item becomes a balance entry sized by its duration. Continued silence into next week, with the refinery running -> the signal deflates to logistics.
changes.delta: New: emergency SPR exchange of up to 400,000 barrels, immediate delivery, cause not stated. Unchanged: posted contracts 133.56 Mbbl to 13 companies; no award for either open round; SPR at about 282.7 Mbbl after a 0.3 Mbbl draw in the week ending Oct 16.
changes.source: DOE press release, energy.gov, Oct 23, 2026, read directly; Reuters, Oct 23 (refiner confirmation; reserve at its lowest since 1982); DOE SPR pages checked Oct 24
changes.title: DOE lent reserve crude to a Gulf Coast refinery on an emergency basis, cause undisclosed

changes.balance: The one traded front-month print of the episode so far is a tightening, printed while the deferred tenors only marked tighter on one-lot and zero-lot volume. The synthetic premium exists only as an untraded mark below both verdict lines: directionally consistent with a supply return, evidentially worth nothing until somebody trades it.
changes.body: Friday's ICE settlement file was not available for this edition, so Canadian differentials carry Thursday's file with its date: WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.85 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 22), up $0.50 on 515 lots, the front month's first traded tightening of the episode, with WCS Houston Dec26 at -$19.35 and the ARV to TMW December spread at +$8.50. Dec26 synthetic crude settled at +$5.70 on Oct 22 on zero volume; the contract has not traded since Oct 13 (+$4.55 on 40 lots), so the pre-registered return verdict against the +$7.00 and +$6.50 lines remains unscored and its window extends to the first settle that actually trades. No public return confirmation for the Syncrude, Horizon or Suncor autumn windows has been published. Third-quarter volumes are the next arbiter: Imperial and Cenovus on Oct 30, Suncor on Nov 3, Vermilion on Nov 4, MEG Energy on Nov 5 (newly confirmed from the company calendar) and Enbridge on Nov 6.
changes.conditional: A traded Dec26 synthetic settle at any level -> the verdict scores against +$7.00 and +$6.50. Friday's ICE file showing a second traded WCS tightening -> the front is unwinding into flat-price strength. Q3 volumes below guided rates -> the return read fails on data, not tape.
changes.delta: Carried: TMW Dec26 -$27.85 on 515 lots (ICE, Oct 22); ARV Dec26 -$19.35; spread +$8.50; TMS Dec26 +$5.70 on zero lots. New: MEG Energy Q3 confirmed for Nov 5. Friday's ICE file lands with Monday's edition.
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD settles, Oct 22, 2026 (most recent file available); MEG Energy events calendar, checked Oct 24; Q3 calendar as confirmed Oct 20 to 22
changes.title: WCS December carries Thursday's traded tightening; the synthetic verdict is still waiting on a traded settle

flags.body: Kpler puts Middle East crude exports at 17.3 Mb/d in October, above the 16.9 pre-war average, with Hormuz flows at 11.7 Mb/d, about 82 percent of pre-war (Oct 22). The maritime security centre counted 12 attacks in and around the Strait last week, a record, and shipping intelligence counts 28 attacks in October. The Revolutionary Guards' claim of seven vessels hit or mined has no named vessel and no independent corroboration after three days, and US Central Command called the mine claims incorrect. In Saudi Arabia, Wednesday's attacks at Shaybah (operations not affected) and Dammam airport (two killed) are confirmed, the national oil company evacuated its Dhahran headquarters on Thursday with no operations disruption reported, and Friday brought unconfirmed Houthi claims against Abha airport and the Jazan refining complex against a third straight day of confirmed coalition interceptions. Trade the flow prints and confirmed incidents, not the claims.
flags.title: Hormuz flows above pre-war on exports; the seven-vessel claim is silent for a third day
flags.trigger: Independent corroboration of any claimed incident, a named vessel, a flow print stepping down, a Saudi statement of facility damage, or an operations impact from the Dhahran evacuation

flags.body: The first tanker under the waiver loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading for New York, arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, shipping data). No signed supply contracts have been confirmed and no further loading has been reported. The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The binding constraint is Russian refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit is halted since Oct 15 with no restart reported, and the largest refiner is stretching repairs from days into months. The import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027 and the waiver has no fixed expiry.
flags.title: Sanctions waiver: first US cargo at sea; contracts unconfirmed; November tranche is the supply test
flags.trigger: A first loading for the November tranche, a named US buyer or signed-contract confirmation, a Ryazan restart report, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). December's nowcast opens at persistence on those levels and no December judgment call is registered yet. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST, and on the published pattern (October's notice Sep 16, November's Oct 20) the December notice is expected around Nov 19 to 20, after nominations close, so the call must be registered as a judgment call rather than read off the notice. WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.85 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 22) on 515 lots, its first traded tightening of the episode.
flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights; December call unregistered; December notice expected after nominations close
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call before Nov 17, a traded December synthetic settle scoring the return verdict, or Friday's ICE file (landing Monday) showing a second traded front-month move

flags.body: Spot fixtures have eased for a second week: a VLCC on Arabian Gulf to China fixed at $29.61 million (Oct 22) against a Gulf to China cost print near a record $37.37 per barrel earlier in the week, Brazil to China at $48 million, and US Gulf to China near $60 million against a $79.6 million October record. The Baltic Exchange Week 43 weekly had not published as of this edition; the last confirmed weekly is Week 42 (Oct 16), TD3C WS 1281.25 (TCE $1,370,193 per day) and TD9 WS 830. A single-source report of a much lower Gulf to China fixture was not carried as a print. At prevailing Caribbean to Gulf levels, freight still forces competing heavy sellers toward deeper FOB offers into the Gulf and pressures WCS Houston; easing at the margin reduces the incremental pressure, it does not shelter Canadian barrels.
flags.title: Freight fixtures are correcting; the Baltic Week 43 weekly has not published
flags.trigger: Publication of the Baltic Week 43 weekly, a verified fixture materially below the $29.61 million print, or a TD9 print confirming the correction has reached the Caribbean to Gulf leg
